task.description: WF-03 Steps 0.5+1+2 for Q-1011 / GH #2311 / ISS-1029: registry lookup, run the repro, root cause, fix design for the three promotion read routes (stored-tenant check), list decision, test update list, draft docs/issues/ISS-1029.yaml. Design only; no lib/ code.

result.summary:
REVISION 3 (rev2 + the CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR r3 findings, step-02-code-design-validator-r3.json; supersedes rev1/rev2 where they conflict; the sections below are the full current design). Source of truth for the contract: the REVISED 10-point ACs of GH #2311 (comment of letflow-2, 2026-10-13T10:53Z) plus the AC6 clarification (GH #2311 comment 6146252089: behaviour not mechanism; in-app chunked filter ACCEPTED BY FILER, no deviation sign-off pending). Diagnosis (root cause, registry, repro) is unchanged from rev1 and measured by the validator at 4daad8ca0 (2/5 passed, 3 failed). WHAT WAS WRONG IN REV1: its read predicate was the write predicate (BOTH stored ids must be the caller's), so a named PARTY (source OR target is the caller's tenant) with a foreign counterpart got the 404 instead of the ISS-1023 own-side 200 view. The four ISS-1021/1023 pinning tests assert exactly that party view and rev1 wrongly flipped them.

SQL EVALUATION (supervisor addendum, done before the filer's clarification landed; recorded for the PR body). Tried on the project's Postgres 16.13 (5462): CASE WHEN v IS JSON OBJECT THEN CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(v::jsonb->'a')='string' THEN lower(v::jsonb->>'a') END END. Measured: 'x', '[1]', '7', 'null', truncated '{"a":', '', whitespace-padded object, nested object, number all return NULL or the value with no error (IS JSON OBJECT is a safe guard against every non-object/invalid shape), duplicate keys take the last (same as Jason). It is NOT total: text that is valid JSON grammar but holds a \u0000 or a lone surrogate escape ('{"a":"\u0000"}', '{"a":"\ud800"}') passes IS JSON and then ::jsonb RAISES (unsupported Unicode escape), which would 500 the whole list; a regex pre-guard on those escapes would be needed and was not completed (the deep-nesting / huge-exponent probes did not finish). Because the filer accepted the in-app filter, the design keeps the store's chunked keyset filter (fail closed, one predicate shared with the per-review routes, no SQL/Elixir divergence on odd JSON). If a stored/generated column is ever wanted it is a separate issue.

THE READ PREDICATE (new, separate from the write predicate; AC1, AC2, AC3, AC7)
Keep review_tenants_authorized?/2 EXACTLY as is for the write routes (approve L572, reject L613, apply L653, run-assertions L788 via stored_tenants_authorized?/3; both-sides strict, unchanged behaviour). Add a private pure fun review_read_access(conn, %PromotionReview{serialised_plan: s}) :: :full | :own_side | :none, used by GET /:id, GET /:id/context and the list:
  1. operator (PlatformTenant.scope_facts_for(conn.assigns.auth_context).platform_scope?, i.e. tenant_view(conn) == :operator) -> :full (never decodes; unreadable rows stay visible to operators, AC7).
  2. plan = Jason.decode(s); {:ok, %{} = m} -> m; anything else -> %{} (never raises: non-bang decode, no ::jsonb).
  3. own_src? / own_tgt? = TenantTarget.authorize_target_tenant(conn, m["source_tenant_id"]) == :ok, same for target (that helper compares a canonical-UUID string to conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id case-insensitively and fails closed on nil, non-binary, slug, non-UUID). The tenant comes ONLY from the authenticated auth_context, never from params/headers/body (AC3).
  4. own_src? and own_tgt? -> :full (own/own, today's behaviour); own_src? xor own_tgt? -> :own_side (a named party with a foreign or unreadable counterpart: the ISS-1023 view); neither (including absent/unreadable ids, a plan that is not a JSON object, truncated JSON) -> :none (non-party, AC2, AC7).
Routes: GET /:id/context: :full | :own_side -> Response.ok(review_context_map(review, tenant_view(conn))) with shape_plan/2 UNCHANGED (it already yields entries [], own-side ids and definition ids only, foreign ids omitted for a non-operator with one foreign side); :none -> Response.not_found(conn). GET /:id: :none -> Response.not_found(conn) BEFORE any assertion-run read; :full -> render_assertion_run as today (7-key map); :own_side -> the SAME existing 7-key run map (ORCH decision, AC5 below). List: row_visible? = fn r -> review_read_access(conn, r) != :none end for non-operators only (operator passes no filter), via the existing PromotionReviewStore.list_reviews/2 :row_visible? keyset scan (chunk max(page_size + 1, 100), no cap, cursor from the last EMITTED row, exhaustion -> nil), which needs NO change. The list item map is the unchanged 7-key allowlist (no plan content).
AC5 DECISION (ORCH, rev3; replaces the rev2 reduced-map idea entirely): GET /:id returns the existing 7-key assertion-run map (run_id, status, sandbox_id, teardown_error, assertions_passed, assertions_failed, failing_assertion_ids) to :full AND :own_side callers. NO new response shape; the original T-8 pinning test context_other_keys_and_status_unchanged (which reads (b -> a) as A and asserts the 7 keys) stays as it is (AC1). Rationale: a non-party now gets the 404, so a party sees strictly less than before ISS-1029 and nothing new is disclosed. RESIDUAL (pre-existing, not introduced here, NOT fixed in this run): the 7-key map carries free-text teardown_error and failing_assertion_ids, which can in principle name the foreign side of a review that has a foreign counterpart. SECURITY-REVIEWER must rule on it and a separate follow-up issue is to be filed for it (status-only or an allowlisted run map for parties); this issue must not change the run map.

AC7 OPERATOR /context DECODE (rev3, validator MAJOR): review_context_map/2 (promotions.ex ~L563) calls Jason.decode!(review.serialised_plan); an unparseable stored text (e.g. truncated '{"a":') raises Jason.DecodeError and 500s the OPERATOR, who by AC7 must see the row. Specify a tolerant decode on that path: replace the bang decode by a private tolerant_plan/1 = case Jason.decode(text) do {:ok, decoded} -> decoded; {:error, _} -> nil end, and keep shape_plan(plan, view) unchanged (operator: pass-through; for a valid non-map JSON value the existing behaviour is unchanged). Degraded context for an unparseable row: HTTP 200, the same nine-key envelope, "serialised_plan": null (JSON null is also what a stored "null" already renders), nothing else changes. Non-operators cannot reach this (unreadable ids -> :none -> 404). GET /:id and the list never decode for the operator, so they cannot 500 on it.

FILER-ACCEPTED MECHANISM, CONDITIONS (a)(b)(c) from the clarification: (a) unreadable stored ids never 500 and are :none for non-operators, :full for the operator: tests 8 and 9 below; (b) no cursor/page boundary exposes, gap-signals or counts a hidden row, including an ALL-HIDDEN page: tests 6, 7, 10; (c) party decided from stored ids vs authenticated tenant, never the request: test 5.

PER-AC -> TEST -> MUTANT TABLE (T# = test in the list below; N# = mutant in the list below)
AC1 party keeps ISS-1023 view (200, own-side fields, entries [], foreign ids omitted; four pinning tests as they are): T1 party reads /context as source and as target; T2 the reverted ISS-1021/1023 pinning tests; N1, N5.
AC2 404 only for non-operator non-party: T3 non-party 404 on /:id and /:id/context (seed b->p in A's schema, and P-held reader of (a,b) in P's schema, pinned and unpinned); T4 operator 200 on all three; N1, N2, N7.
AC3 party from stored ids vs authenticated tenant, never the request: T5 request carries query tenant_id/source_tenant_id/target_tenant_id (and an X-Tenant-Id style header) naming the reader's own tenant on a non-party review, or a foreign tenant on a party review: outcome unchanged; N3.
AC4 same status and body as nonexistent id on all three routes, byte for byte: T3 compares Scope.observable (status, headers, body) of the foreign-named review to a fresh nonexistent id on /:id and /:id/context; T6 list: the non-operator list response with hidden rows present equals, on the SAME observable tuple (status + headers + body, same conn fixture so trace_id matches, as in the existing baseline helper), the response after the hidden rows are deleted (cursor-less page; for a cursor page compare status, headers, decoded ids and inserted_at, since the cursor mint time differs); N14, N13.
AC5 party keeps the existing run map, no new shape: T7 party (:own_side, (b -> a) and (a -> b)) GET /:id with a recorded run: 200 and EXACTLY the existing 7 keys (same key set and values as the own/own read); the original T-8 context_other_keys_and_status_unchanged passes untouched; N6 (reduced/new map for a party) and N6b (non-party gets the map). The teardown_error / failing_assertion_ids residual is recorded for SECURITY-REVIEWER and a separate issue, not tested away.
AC6 list omits non-parties for non-operators, no placeholder (mechanism accepted by filer): T8 list contains :own and :party rows, omits :none rows, no placeholder keys; N7a (placeholder), N3b (filter dropped).
AC7 unreadable ids: non-party for non-operators (hidden, never 500), visible to operator, never a 500 for ANY caller: T9 list + /:id + /:id/context with rows overwritten to "x", [1], 7, null, "s", empty text, truncated JSON '{"a":', object missing ids, ids non-string: non-operator 200 list showing only own rows, per-review routes 404 bytes of nonexistent; operator list includes them, operator /:id answers 200 and operator /:id/context answers 200 with serialised_plan null for the unparseable texts (valid non-map JSON keeps its decoded value); N8, N9, N10, N10b (bang decode left in review_context_map).
AC8 no gaps, no counts, page-boundary test: T10 hidden rows interleaved at page boundaries with page_size 1 and 2 (patterns V H V, H H V V, V H H) incl. an ALL-HIDDEN page schema (items [] and next_cursor nil) and a visible row behind a hidden run of more than two chunks (>250) returned by the first request; decode every cursor: none contains a hidden id or inserted_at; no empty page has a cursor; union of pages == visible set once each; N11, N12, N15, N16.
AC9 SECURITY-REVIEWER before TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR: routing below (process gate, no test).
AC10 failing case re-seeded with a NON-party caller so it exercises the 404 path: T11 the repro file's describe "non-operator reader, review naming a foreign tenant" is reseeded (b, p) in A's schema (was (a, b) = a party); a party control (a, b) and (b, a) expecting 200 is ADDED; mutant N1 kills it.

TESTS (rev2 set; all in test/letflow/routers/ unless stated)
T1-T11 above go into promotion_read_stored_ids_test.exs (the repro file, reworked): seed_ordered!/3 changes its :hidden kind from (own source, foreign target) = a PARTY under rev2 to (foreign source b, foreign target p) = non-party, and gains kinds :party_src (own, foreign) and :party_tgt (foreign, own). Every rev1 describe 1(a)..1(i) that used :hidden keeps its assertions but now means non-party. Existing tests kept: nonexistent baseline, own/own control, operator control.
Plus store level (promotion_review_store_test.exs row_visible? tests): unchanged, the store stays predicate-agnostic.
Write-route guard: promotion_approve_reject_stored_ids_test.exs and promotion_scope_test.exs item 7 stay UNCHANGED and must still pass (a party with a foreign counterpart is still refused on approve/reject/apply/run-assertions); verify they contain a one-own-side case, and add one (a, b) case to promotion_approve_reject_stored_ids_test.exs if absent, to kill N4.

REV1-FLIPPED TESTS THAT REVERT (exact; HEAD 7ec02d70 vs original d2e08c67b):
 promotion_context_shaping_test.exs: context_omits_foreign_tenant_ids_for_non_operator (restore the original body: seed (b -> a) read by A, 200, shaped target_tenant_id == a, source_tenant_id absent, source_definition_id absent, target_definition_id kept, entries [] etc.); context_other_keys_and_status_unchanged (restore seed ctx.b -> ctx.a).
 promotion_context_allowlist_test.exs: foreign_side_definition_id_omitted_own_side_kept (restore the original four-case table for (b,a), (a,a), (a,b); the (b,b) case CHANGES to a 404 because it is a non-party, not a revert); null_definition_id_omitted_for_foreign_side_kept_for_own_side (restore seed b -> a and its assertions); envelope_has_nine_keys_for_both_views (restore the loop [ctx.a, ctx.p] with (b, fixture.tenant_id)); pin_unset_would_be_operator_is_shaped_like_everyone_else (restore the original: unpinned P reading (b -> p), 200, source_tenant_id absent, target == p, entries []; the rev1 own-review extras may stay).
 promotion_context_entries_scope_test.exs: one_foreign_side_is_enough_to_withhold_entries (restore: (p,b) and (b,p) read by P unpinned are 200 with entries [], markers refuted, allowlist subset; keep the P/P control).
 promotions_test.exs: req397_sample_plan/2 source_tenant_id back to Ecto.UUID.generate() (the caller is the target = a party; the R12 list tests must pass with NO helper change).
 legacy_plans_with_missing_or_non_binary_tenant_ids_fail_closed (entries_scope L292) is SPLIT, not flipped wholesale (validator MAJOR, measured): keep the ORIGINAL loop assertions (200, entries [], no marker) for every case with at least ONE readable own id, because those are parties: 'source missing', 'target missing', 'foreign source, own target', 'own source, foreign target', every 'source <bad value>' / 'target <bad value>' case whose other side is own, and the whitespace/empty-source variants (target own). Only 'both ids missing', 'both foreign' and 'odd keys only' become the nonexistent-review 404 (assert Scope.observable equals the nonexistent id's, and no LEGACY-MARKER / n-iss1023-legacy / b in the body). The own/own positive control and the operator half stay unchanged.
 STAY flipped (non-party, or id-less/unreadable = non-party under AC7, so still the nonexistent 404): promotion_context_shaping_test none; promotion_context_allowlist_test.exs non_map_plan_fails_closed, legacy_plan_missing_keys, non_scalar_under_plain_key_omitted (own ids added, because its stored plan has no ids), entries_not_a_list_replaced_by_empty_list (own ids added; the exact-equality expectation becomes plan == %{"process_key" => "p", "source_tenant_id" => a, "target_tenant_id" => a, "entries" => []} for each bad entries value, since shape_plan keeps own ids; this is what the rev1 file already asserts), plus the (b,b) row of foreign_side_definition_id...; promotion_context_entries_scope_test.exs foreign_reviews_entries_are_empty_for_a_non_operator_reader_in_p ((b,c), (c,b), (b,b) read by P: P is a party of none), withheld_entries_leave_the_rest_of_the_response_unchanged (review (b -> a) read by P: non-party), tenant_admin_of_the_platform_tenant_reads_a_foreign_review_without_entries ((b -> a) in P's schema read by P's TENANT_ADMIN: non-party; pinned and unpinned stay 404).
 test/specs: ISS-1021.md and ISS-1023.md rev1 notes ('shaping is now defence in depth behind the 404') are rewritten: shaping stays LIVE for parties; the 404 applies to non-parties only. test/specs/ISS-1029.md rewritten to the table above. Decision 0046 (~L470) follow-up text must describe the party rule.

MUTANTS (each applied alone must fail the named tests)
N1 read predicate requires BOTH ids own (rev1/write predicate) -> T1, T11 party controls, the reverted pinning tests. N2 predicate true when either id is merely present/binary (not compared to the tenant) -> T3, T11, T10. N3 party decided from a request param/header/body -> T5. N3b list filter dropped -> T8, T10. N4 write routes switched to the party predicate -> promotion_approve_reject_stored_ids_test (+ the added (a,b) case), promotion_scope_test item 7. N5 party sees foreign ids or entries (shape_plan bypassed) -> reverted pinning tests T-8/T-11/T-13. N6 :own_side /:id returns a reduced or otherwise new run map (the rev2 four-key shape) -> T7 and the untouched T-8 context_other_keys_and_status_unchanged. N6b non-party receives the run map -> T3. N7 operator filtered or 404'd -> T4, operator list/context controls. N7a placeholder instead of omit -> T8, T6. N8 unreadable stored ids treated as party/visible (fail open) for non-operators -> T9. N9 predicate raises on unreadable JSON (Jason.decode!) -> T9 (list 500). N10 operator's unreadable row hidden or 500 -> T9 operator half. N10b Jason.decode! left in review_context_map -> T9 operator /:id/context on '{"a":' (MEASURED: DecodeError, 1/2 failed in the verification run). N11 next_cursor from last scanned row -> T10 cursor decode. N12 scan cap reintroduced -> T10 long hidden run. N13 non-party 404 differs in body (extra detail, 403) -> T3. N14 list body differs from the hidden-rows-deleted list (count/total field, placeholder) -> T6. N15 gap: the +1 hidden row skipped or duplicated at a boundary -> T10. N16 empty page with non-nil cursor or short page with a cursor -> T10.

RISKS: (R1) the 7-key run map is returned to parties with a foreign counterpart: free-text teardown_error / failing_assertion_ids are a PRE-EXISTING property (unchanged by this issue); SECURITY-REVIEWER to rule, follow-up issue to be filed, no change in this run. (R2) a party reading /context still sees def_id/process_key and requested_by of a review naming a foreign counterpart: process_key is documented allowed (ISS-1023 R4/R8), requested_by is an actor id; unchanged from before ISS-1029. (R3) a plan with exactly one readable own id and an unreadable other is :own_side by AC3 (source OR target == tenant), shaped by the existing allowlist. (R4) per-request full scan for non-operators, no cap (rev1 trade-off stands). (R5) the PR is already draft (#2474) with rev1 behaviour: ELIXIR-DEV rework touches only promotions.ex (new review_read_access/2, the three call sites, reduced run map) and tests; the store is untouched.

ROUTING (AC9): CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR on this rev2 -> ELIXIR-DEV (promotions.ex) + TEST-DESIGNER (tests above) -> SECURITY-REVIEWER (BEFORE TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR) -> REVIEWER -> TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR -> TEST-RUNNER (Postgres 5462: LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED=1 MIX_ENV=test mix test <file>, one mix process) -> RELEASE-VALIDATOR.

REV3 VERIFICATION (measured by the ISSUE-FIXER on this branch, Postgres 5462, one mix process, the validator's method): the rev1 lib was patched TEMPORARILY with (i) review_read_access(conn, review) :: :full | :own_side | :none (operator -> :full; else authorize_target_tenant on stored source/target, both -> :full, one -> :own_side, none -> :none) used by /:id, /:id/context and the list row_visible?, and (ii) tolerant_plan/1 in review_context_map; the four ORIGINAL test files (d2e08c67b) were restored, plus promotion_approve_reject_stored_ids_test.exs and a temporary operator/party test. Result: 56/65 passed; the 9 failures are exactly the STAYS-flipped set (entries_scope: tenant_admin_of_the_platform_tenant..., foreign_reviews_entries_are_empty..., withheld_entries_leave_the_rest..., legacy_plans_with_missing_or_non_binary_tenant_ids_fail_closed [whole loop; passes once split as specified]; allowlist: legacy_plan_missing_keys, non_scalar_under_plain_key_omitted, entries_not_a_list_replaced_by_empty_list, foreign_side_definition_id_omitted_own_side_kept [(b,b) row], non_map_plan_fails_closed). context_other_keys_and_status_unchanged (7-key map), context_omits_foreign_tenant_ids_for_non_operator, null_definition_id..., envelope_has_nine_keys..., pin_unset_..., one_foreign_side_is_enough..., every promotions_test.exs R12 test with the ORIGINAL helper, and the ISS-1026 write-route tests all PASSED unmodified. The temporary test: operator /context, /:id and list answered 200 for unparseable texts ('{"a":', 'x', '[1]', '7', 'null', '"s"', ''), non-operator list 200 and /context 404; a mutant with Jason.decode! restored in review_context_map made it fail with Jason.DecodeError (N10b killed). lib/ and test/ were then reverted with git checkout HEAD; the branch carries no lib/ or test/ change from this experiment (only handoff + issue file).
